messages:
jane_support: :rotating_light: ACME (acme-prod) hitting 502s on hosted inference /v1/generate since ~10:12 UTC. Customer says spikes coincide with heavy batch jobs. sample request_id=req_0a1b2c3d. They included curl + response codes.
ben_oncall: looking. any control-plane traces or upstream errors? pinging infra.
carol_eng: can you paste a couple request_ids? I'll grep gateway and routing-policy logs.
jane_support: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0f9e8d7c. They also reported increased latency and retry storms, billing spike possibly from retries.
infra_bot: alert: configdb-pool errors increased x8 at 10:11:23 UTC. auth-service started returning 504 -> configdb timeout. (auto-alert #cfgdb-conn-fault)
ben_oncall: seeing same in control-plane dashboards. routing-policy service shows 504s and then 502 from gateway when routing fails.
carol_eng: paste of relevant routing-policy log (truncated):
```
2026-03-17T10:11:25Z routing-policy svc_id=rp-3 level=error msg="configdb query timeout" err="deadline exceeded"
2026-03-17T10:11:26Z auth svc_id=auth-2 level=warn msg="kv handshake failed" err="conn pool exhausted"
2026-03-17T10:11:27Z gateway svc_id=gateway-1 level=error msg="upstream rpc error" code=502 route_id=tenant-acme
```
mike_prod: quick diag — last deploy to control-plane at 09:50 included configdb client bump to v2.3 (pooling change). Could be regresssion.
ben_oncall: repro with curl (from inside control-plane network):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"control_plane_error","detail":"routing_policy_unavailable"}
```
carol_eng: I can reproduce locally against staging configdb by driving connections, yields timeout around pool limit. suspect connection leak or pool size too small after v2.3.
jane_support: customer wants ETA. they reported 1200 requests failed across a 7 minute window.
ben_oncall: mitigation idea: enable routing-policy local cache/fallback for tenant-level policy and scale configdb read replicas, and bump pool size temporarily. I'll run a controlled restart of routing-policy in canary to pick up cached fallback.
carol_eng: agree. I'll push a hotfix that falls back to last-known-policy if configdb times out. prepping PR now.
deploy_bot: scheduled rolling restart: routing-policy (canary) at 10:28 UTC.
infra_bot: increased configdb read pool on replicas db-r1,db-r2 by +30 connections at 10:30 UTC.
ben_oncall: monitoring — 10:33 UTC errors drop to baseline. gateway 502s stop. informing customer.
jane_support: told ACME support team the short-term mitigations and that we'll follow up with a postmortem. they acknowledged and asked about billing credits for retry charges.
mike_prod: open ticket for billing review. tag finance and support. also reverting v2.3 client to v2.2 is on the table if leak repro confirmed.
carol_eng: PR merged for fallback cache, will roll out canary across 3 pods then full. Logs show no new conn-exhaustion after pool bump.
ben_oncall: closing incident once customer verifies. moving to postmortem channel for root cause and long-term fixes (connection pooling metrics, configdb circuit breaker, routing-policy resilient cache).
jane_support: ACME confirmed behavior normalizing at 10:40 UTC and no more failed requests. they asked for postmortem and billing consideration. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
mike_prod: follow-ups: (1) postmortem doc, (2) revert or patch v2.3 client, (3) add alert for configdb pool exhaustion and per-tenant retry amplification, (4) billing review.
carol_eng: adding repro steps to issue: heavy parallel requests to control-plane auth/routing endpoints until pool fills. sample script attached to ticket.
jane_support: created customer ticket #INC-2026-0423 and internal incident #IRT-2026-1004. will post postmortem link here when ready.
